segments.t: On first launch, korTTY asks you to create a KTPH000master passwordKTPH001. This password encrypts all stored connection passwords, SSH key passphrases and credentials using KTPH002AES-256-GCMKTPH003.

Enter a password (minimum 6 characters). The field border turns KTPH000greenKTPH001 when long enough and KTPH002redKTPH003 when too short; a strength indicator rates the quality. A weak or common password shows a warning but can still be used if you confirm.

Leave KTPH000Share anonymous usage statisticsKTPH001 ticked to help improve korTTY, or clear the checkbox if you would rather share nothing. It is pre-selected, but the choice is yours before you confirm — what is collected is fully anonymous and GDPR-compliant, and the setting can be changed any time in KTPH002Settings → PrivacyKTPH003. The KTPH004?KTPH005 button opens KTPH006Anonymous data for application optimizationKTPH007. An organization policy that forbids telemetry locks the checkbox and leaves it clear.
On subsequent launches you are prompted to enter the master password to unlock your encrypted data.

KTPH000Settings → SecurityKTPH001 offers two ways to skip the prompt. Turning off KTPH002Require master password on startupKTPH003 hides the prompt and starts korTTY with the vault locked: stored passwords and keys stay unavailable until you choose KTPH004Configuration → Security → Unlock Vault…KTPH005 or click KTPH006Unlock Vault…KTPH007 in any "vault locked" message. KTPH008Disable master password prompt on startup (auto-login)KTPH009 instead unlocks the vault automatically from a copy of your master password kept on disk. That copy is encrypted only with a key built into korTTY, not with your master password, so it guards against casual disclosure only; reserve this option for throwaway or test environments. See the KTPH010Security settingsKTPH011 for details, including unattended first launches that skip the setup dialog entirely.
AES-256-GCM with a key built into korTTY, not your master password; owner-only file permissions

AES-256-GCM (master-password-derived key); written only while KTPH000Also restore the output of each terminal pane (encrypted)KTPH001 is enabled under KTPH002Settings → Window → Session RestoreKTPH003, and nothing is written while the vault is locked
See the KTPH000Security referenceKTPH001 for the full encryption and backup model.
